messages:
elaine: Heads-up — I want to lock a rollout plan for the tenant-priority feature. Goal: route high-value tenants to Dedicated pools with graceful degradation back to shared instances if capacity/latency degrades. Need canary/progression steps, A/B for cost vs quality, and a fallback matrix.

mike: Do we have a rough definition of 'high-value'? list or tag?

elaine: Customer list = top 20 by ARR for Q1 + a small opt-in cohort. We'll surface an allowlist tag `tenant.priority:high`.

sanju: Suggest we do a sequential sparse canary first: 1% of high tenants (by session count) -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%. Each step 24h with metrics gate. Keeps blast radius tiny.

tess: For gated metrics, what thresholds? latency p95, error rate, and cost delta?

mike: Propose gates: p95 increase <= 10% vs baseline, 5xx errors delta <= 0.1%, and cost per 1k tokens delta <= 15% (since Dedicated may be cheaper but initial routing overhead could bump cost).

elaine: +1. Also include successful inference quality check: sampling of outputs for a small eval set. If model variant changes, require quality A/B test (we can run shadow traffic comparisons).

sanju: Implementation notes — feature flag naming: `ff/tenant-priority/v1` with metadata: {"allowlist":"tenant.priority:high","mode":"canary","pool":"dedicated-v2"}. We'll need infra to support per-tenant routing keys.

mike: infra-bot: preflight checklist created -> runbook link: https://internal.redwood/infrarunbooks/tenant-priority.

infra-bot: preflight status: GPU pool capacity check OK, extra warm replicas queued, KV-tags available, circuit-breaker hooks registered.

elaine: Real-world scenarios: if Dedicated pool latency rises, we fallback to shared with degraded QoS but keep service on. Fallback priority: dedicated -> regional-shared -> global-shared.

tess: How do we detect Dedicated pool degradation? Metrics: queue depth > 100 for > 2m OR p95 > SLA threshold OR consecutive rate-limited errors > 50 in 5m.

sanju: Add automatic cooling policy: if fallback triggers, reduce canary by 50% and notify oncall. After stabilizing for 30m, try a soft-rollforward by moving 10% back.

mike: For A/B: we should split some high tenants to Dedicated variant A and shared variant B to measure quality and cost. But careful: customers might notice performance differences. Limit A/B to internal canary tenants or opt-ins.

elaine: Agreed. Public customers get routing opt-in. For CA/B work, use internal beta tenants and a few friendly customers who signed NDA.

tess: Observability: per-tenant dashboard for latency/cost/quality, alerts for gate failures, and an automated regression test run after each step. Need traces that include routing decision tag.

mike: We'll add routing tags: `route.variant`, `route.pool`, and `route.reason` to spans. Also log `flag.eval_version` on every request.

sanju: Small config snippet for the rollout stage (for the engineering playbook):
```
{
  "flag": "ff/tenant-priority/v1",
  "stages": [
    {"name":"sparse-canary","percent":1,"duration":"24h","gates":["latency","errors","cost"]},
    {"name":"small","percent":5,"duration":"24h"},
    {"name":"ramp","percent":20,"duration":"48h"},
    {"name":"full","percent":100,"duration":"-"}
  ]
}
```

elaine: Nice. Ops question: who owns the kill-switch?

mike: Oncall owns the emergency kill-switch. Product owns the rollout steps and approval. Engineering (infra) owns automated fallback behavior.

tess: We also need a customer comms template if we proactively move them to Dedicated (billing, SLA differences). I'll draft one.

elaine: Launch criteria (high level):
- Preflight green (capacity + runbook)
- Canary gate pass for 48h across p95, errors, quality checks
- Oncall + product sign-off
- Customer comms prepared

sanju: Post-launch: monitor cost delta weekly and auto-eval quality drift. If quality drift > threshold, auto-fallback and open regression ticket.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for 2751234580 by infra on Mon 08:00 UTC.

mike: Quick timeline: preflight this week, sparse canary Mon, small Tue, ramp Wed, hold until Friday for biz sign-off.

elaine: Action items:
- sanju: add routing tags + implement auto-cooldown (ETA Wed)
- tess: draft customer comms + internal FAQ (ETA Wed)
- mike: verify capacity + prepare runbook edits (ETA Fri)
- product: finalize allowlist and legal sign-offs (ETA Thu)

tess: tagging docs with `#rollout` and I'll ping ops when comms ready :thumbsup:

elaine: Thanks — will follow up with the final flagged config and a short shiproom at Thu 16:00.

mike: :rocket:

infra-bot: update: canary started at 2751234580, 1 tenant in sparse group. Monitoring hooks active.

elaine: Closing loop — if anyone sees unexpected noise, call the oncall immediately.

mike: copy that.
